subject: sociology
title: Mapping the Big Theories
welcome_lead: Step into the great hall of sociology and meet the rival schools of thought that explain why society sticks together — or pulls apart.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on the foundations of sociological theory: functionalism, Marxism, feminism, interactionism and postmodernism.
final_note: You can now name the four classic theories and one modern challenger. That is the backbone of every sociology essay.

concepts.def: View that society works through shared values and agreement.
View that society is shaped by struggle between unequal groups.
Looks at whole-society structures like class or institutions.
Forces in society that shape how people behave.
The ability of individuals to make their own choices.

walkthroughs.body_html: Functionalists like Durkheim see society as glued together by shared values — this is consensus. Marxists see society as split by class conflict between the bourgeoisie and proletariat — this is conflict. Feminists add a second conflict: men versus women under patriarchy.

Macro theories (functionalism, Marxism, feminism) zoom out to whole structures. Micro theories like interactionism zoom in: Mead and Goffman ask how meanings are built in everyday interaction, like a job interview or classroom chat.

Postmodernists such as Lyotard and Bauman argue the big theories are outdated 'metanarratives'. Today identity is fragmented, fluid and shaped by media and consumer choice rather than fixed class or gender roles.
